accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: Rent payer — only covers rent for the policy (and optional
ValidationPda) accounts. Receives rent back on delete. This
account is NOT the recipient. See
reports/B3-fee-payer-becomes-recipient-without-gateway-signer-constraint.md

accounts.name: recipient
docs: an authority — the corresponding output-mint ATA is derived and
validated at execute time (`recipient_token_account.owner ==
composable_policy.recipient`). Must be non-default to prevent
accidental burn-to-nowhere policies. Mirrors the pattern in
`create_payment_policy::CreatePaymentPolicy::recipient`.

accounts.name: validation_program
docs: Pass SystemProgram when no validation is configured.

accounts.name: input_mint
docs: Forward input mint. Pinned against `forward_config.input_mint`
in the handler (Anchor constraints can't reach handler args) and
fully validated via `validate_mint_compatible` to reject Token-2022
TransferHook / PermanentDelegate / ConfidentialTransferMint etc.
that would break `transfer_checked` at execute time or drain the
PDA-owned intermediate ATA. See reports/L-02-mint-validation-call-sites-incomplete.md
and shared-base §17/§23.

accounts.name: output_mint
docs: Forward output mint. Pinned against `forward_config.output_mint`
in the handler and validated the same way as `input_mint`.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: corresponding tokenAccount/ata will be derived during execution.

accounts.name: gateway
docs: The gateway this referral account belongs to

accounts.name: rent_payer
docs: Only used when stored rent_payer != Pubkey::default().

accounts.name: rent_payer
docs: Only used when stored rent_payer != Pubkey::default().

accounts.name: fee_payer
docs: Fee payer / caller. The trusted three (`gateway.signer` /
`user_payment.owner` / `composable_policy.recipient`) always pass.
Any other signer is admitted ONLY when the gateway has the
ADR-0016 permissionless bit set (cold relayer). The
caller-conditional gate (mandatory min_output_amount for cold
relayers) is enforced in the handler — Anchor constraints can't
express "depends on the policy's forward_config".

accounts.name: user_payment
docs: UserPayment PDA — the delegate on the user's source token account.
It signs ONLY the initial pull (Step 3, user → intermediate). The
intermediate ATAs are owned by the ComposablePolicy PDA (see above),
which signs all other CPIs; this keeps user-source authority
decoupled from intermediate authority.
The user's source token account MUST delegate to this PDA.

accounts.name: validation_program
docs: Pass SystemProgram when the policy has no validation configured.

accounts.name: validation_pda
docs: ValidationPda — typed-deserialised in the handler when validation
is enabled (validation_program != SystemProgram). When validation
is disabled, the account does not exist on-chain and is left
untouched. The address is verified against program-derived seeds
before any bytes are read. See ADR-0016.

accounts.name: user_token_account
docs: User's source token account. Must be owned by the user
(user_payment.owner) and have either the UserPayment PDA (v1)
or the global payments_delegate PDA (v0) set as delegate with
`delegated_amount >= input_amount`.

accounts.name: mint
docs: Input mint (== forward_config.input_mint == user_payment.token_mint).

accounts.name: output_mint
docs: Output mint (== forward_config.output_mint). Required for the
`transfer_checked` calls on the output leg (fees + sweep).

accounts.name: intermediate_input_token_account
docs: UserPayment PDA's intermediate input token account (input_mint ATA).
Created via CPI if non-existent; closed at end to reclaim rent for
the fee_payer.

accounts.name: intermediate_output_token_account
docs: UserPayment PDA's intermediate output token account (output_mint ATA).
Same account as the input when input_mint == output_mint.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: Recipient destination. In normal mode this is the recipient's
output-mint ATA (mint+owner validated in the handler). In
NATIVE_OUTPUT mode (forward_flags bit 0) it is the recipient's
**system wallet** — `closeAccount` ships the WSOL value there as
native SOL. Anchor constraints can't be conditional, so this is
an `UncheckedAccount` and the handler replicates the two original
checks (`mint == output_mint`, `owner == recipient`) in normal
mode. Do NOT weaken the normal-mode checks. See bean
tributary-hgp7 + reports/native-output-sweep.md.

accounts.name: gateway_fee_account
docs: Gateway fee account (output_mint).

accounts.name: protocol_fee_account
docs: Protocol fee account (output_mint).

accounts.name: program_data
docs: Enforces that only the upgrade authority can initialize the protocol.

types.name: ComposableExecuted
docs: An event that is thrown when a composable policy is executed

fields.name: policy_type
docs: Reuses the same `PolicyType` enum as `PaymentPolicy`. Before
unification this was a separate `ScheduleType`; the two were
byte-identical duplicates (see `reports/M-04-inconsistent-month-arithmetic.md`
for the consolidation rationale).

types.name: ComposablePolicyCreated
docs: An event that is thrown when a composable policy is created

types.name: ComposablePolicyDeleted
docs: An event that is thrown when a composable policy is deleted

types.name: ComposablePolicyStatusChanged
docs: An event that is thrown when a composable policy status is changed

fields.name: min_output_amount
docs: Minimum acceptable **net** output the recipient must receive,
measured AFTER gateway and protocol fees have been deducted
from the forward program's gross output. Matches DeFi convention
(Uniswap/Jupiter `amountOutMin`). Set to `None` or `Some(0)` to
disable the check. See
`reports/M5-min-output-amount-checked-before-fees.md`.

types.name: GatewayFeeBpsChanged
docs: An event that is thrown when a gateway fee bps is changed

types.name: GatewayFeeRecipientChanged
docs: An event that is thrown when a gateway fee recipient is changed

types.name: GatewaySignerChanged
docs: An event that is thrown when a gateway signer is changed

types.name: PaymentFrequency
docs: Defines frequency at which recurring payments should occur.
Predefined intervals are provided for common use cases, with Custom
allowing arbitrary intervals defined in seconds.

types.name: PaymentGateway
docs: A payment gateway operated by a service provider that executes recurring payments.
Gateway operators can charge fees for their service and are responsible for
triggering payment execution. Each gateway has an authority (owner), fee recipient,
and signer key used to execute payments on behalf of users.

fields.name: authority
docs: Authority key that owns this gateway. Cannot be changed after creation.

fields.name: fee_recipient
docs: Key that receives gateway fees from processed payments

fields.name: gateway_fee_bps
docs: Gateway fee in basis points (bps). Max 10,000 (100%)

fields.name: is_active
docs: Whether this gateway is active and can process payments

fields.name: padding1
docs: No-longer-used, take care of tumbstone

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix timestamp when gateway was created

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed for address derivation

fields.name: name
docs: Human-readable gateway name (32 bytes max)

fields.name: url
docs: Gateway service URL (64 bytes max)

fields.name: signer
docs: Signer key authorized to execute payments for this gateway

fields.name: feature_flags
docs: Gateway-scoped feature flags (bit-vector)
Bit 0: Referral program enabled (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled)
Bit 1: Net amount mode (1 = net, 0 = gross/default)
Bit 2: Custom protocol fee enabled (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled)
Bit 3: Permissionless composable execution enabled (ADR-0016 —
admits third-party schedulers for conforming composable
policies; trusted caller path unchanged)

fields.name: referral_allocation_bps
docs: What percentage of the **gateway fee** funds the referral pool.
Units: basis points of the gateway fee. Range: 0..=2500.
- 0    = referral program inactive (no pool is carved out)
- 1000 = 10% of the gateway fee becomes the referral pool
- 2500 = 25% of the gateway fee (hard cap)
The remaining `(10000 - referral_allocation_bps)` bps of the gateway fee
stays with the gateway fee recipient.

fields.name: referral_tiers_bps
docs: How the referral pool is split across the 3 chain levels
`[level1 (direct referrer), level2, level3]`. Units: basis points of the
**referral pool** (NOT of the gateway fee). Must sum to 10000 (100%).
Example: with `referral_allocation_bps = 1000` and
`referral_tiers_bps = [5000, 3000, 2000]`, the actual cut of the gateway
fee is L1 = 5%, L2 = 3%, L3 = 2% (each tier_bps × allocation / 10000).
Misreading these as "bps of gateway fee per level" overpays by 10x.

fields.name: custom_protocol_share_bps
docs: Custom protocol share in basis points (bps). Only used if
FEATURE_CUSTOM_PROTOCOL_FEE is set. Overrides the global
`protocol_share_bps` from `ProgramConfig` for this gateway.
Units: share of the gateway fee (not bps-of-payment).
May be zero (subsidise a strategic partner).

fields.name: scheduler_share_bps
docs: Scheduler share in basis points (bps) of the gateway fee.
Per-gateway, gateway-authority-set. Pays the execute-tx signer.

fields.name: padding
docs: Padding for future fields

types.name: PaymentGatewayDeleted

types.name: PaymentPolicy
docs: This structure connects a UserPayment (user/mint) with a Policy, a Gateway.
This is structure that actually specifies subscription payment as you would
expect from an invoice. The SDK would setup these PaymentPolicy

fields.name: user_payment
docs: Reference to the UserPayment account this policy belongs to

fields.name: recipient
docs: Recipient who receives payments

fields.name: gateway
docs: Payment gateway responsible for executing this policy

fields.name: policy_type
docs: Type and parameters of this payment policy

fields.name: status
docs: Current status of this payment policy (Active | Paused | Completed).
`Completed` is terminal and set only by the program when the policy is
exhausted; owners may only toggle Active<->Paused.

fields.name: memo
docs: Human-readable memo/description (64 bytes max)

fields.name: total_paid
docs: Total amount paid out under this policy (cumulative)

fields.name: payment_count
docs: Number of payments executed under this policy

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix timestamp when policy was created

fields.name: updated_at
docs: Unix timestamp when policy was last updated

fields.name: policy_id
docs: Unique identifier for this policy within user_payment scope

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed for address derivation

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: Account that paid rent for this account (receives rent on close)

fields.name: padding
docs: Reserved space for future extensions

types.name: PaymentPolicyCreated
docs: An event that is thrown when a payment policy is created

types.name: PaymentPolicyDeleted
docs: An event that is thrown when a payment policy is deleted

types.name: PaymentPolicyStatusChanged
docs: An event that is thrown when a payment policy status is changed

types.name: PaymentRecord
docs: An event that is thrown when a payment takes place

fields.name: record_id
docs: Post-increment payment counter. For the Nth execution of a policy,
`record_id == N` (starts at 1, not 0). The increment happens inside
`strategy.execute()` (`policies/traits.rs`) before `should_pause_policy`
runs, so `Subscription::max_renewals` ceilings are honored exactly.
Indexers that assumed 0-indexed records must add 1 to historical data
or use `payment_count - 1` for backward display.

types.name: PolicyType
docs: The PolicyType enum implements different payment schemes. The initial policy
will be a subscription payment that enables regular payment according to
a schedule.
IMPORTANT: All variants MUST be exactly 128 bytes to ensure consistent account sizing
and enable future enum variant additions without breaking existing accounts.

types.name: ProgramConfig
docs: This is a unique global program configuration managed by an admin that
defines protocol fees and potentially more.

fields.name: admin
docs: Admin authority that can update protocol configuration

fields.name: fee_recipient
docs: Key that receives protocol fees from all payments

fields.name: protocol_share_bps
docs: Protocol share of the gateway fee in basis points (bps). Max 10,000 (100%).
This is the global default; per-gateway override via FEATURE_CUSTOM_PROTOCOL_FEE.

fields.name: _deprecated
docs: DEPRECATED: Maximum number of active policies allowed per user. Attention tumbstone!

fields.name: emergency_pause
docs: Emergency pause flag - when true, all payments are blocked

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed for address derivation

fields.name: padding
docs: Reserved space for future extensions

types.name: ProgramConfigCreated
docs: An event that is thrown when program is initialized

types.name: ReferralAccount
docs: A referral account that tracks referral codes and chain relationships for reward distribution.
Each referral account is scoped to a specific gateway to enable gateway-specific referral ecosystems.
The PDA derivation uses gateway pubkey and referral_code to ensure uniqueness:
PDA seeds: ["referral", gateway_pubkey, referral_code]
Uses zero_copy for efficient mutable access during payment execution.

fields.name: gateway
docs: The gateway this referral account belongs to (for PDA derivation and scoping)

fields.name: owner
docs: Authority who owns this referral code and can earn rewards

fields.name: referral_code
docs: 6-character alphanumeric referral code

fields.name: _padding_code
docs: Padding for alignment (referrer is 32 bytes, needs 8-byte alignment)

fields.name: referrer
docs: Referrer who brought this user (for chain traversal). Might be the default Pubkey

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix timestamp when account was created

fields.name: total_earned
docs: Total rewards earned by this referrer (in smallest token units)

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed

types.name: ReferralRewardDistributedRecord
docs: An event that is thrown when referral rewards are distributed

types.name: UpdateGatewayReferralSettingsArgs
docs: Arguments for updating gateway referral settings

fields.name: feature_flags
docs: Optional feature flags to update (bit 0 = referral program enabled, bit 1 = net mode)
Bit 2 (custom protocol fee) is reserved for protocol admin and cannot be modified here

fields.name: referral_allocation_bps
docs: Optional referral allocation in basis points (0-2500).
Bps of the **gateway fee** that funds the referral pool.

fields.name: referral_tiers_bps
docs: Optional referral tier distribution `[level1, level2, level3]` in bps.
Bps of the **referral pool** (not the gateway fee); must sum to 10000.
Effective per-level share of the gateway fee = tier_bps × allocation / 10000.

types.name: UserPayment
docs: Each owner/authority+mint has a unique UserPayment account.
The purpose of this account is to be able to identify quickly
some statistics that are valid across *all* payment policies
for an authority across a mint.

fields.name: owner
docs: Owner of this payment account (the user)

fields.name: token_account
docs: Associated token account for payment token

fields.name: token_mint
docs: Mint address of token used for payments

fields.name: active_policies_count
docs: Number of active payment policies for this user/mint combination

fields.name: created_at
docs: Unix timestamp when account was created

fields.name: updated_at
docs: Unix timestamp when account was last updated

fields.name: is_active
docs: Whether this payment account is active

fields.name: bump
docs: PDA bump seed for address derivation

fields.name: created_policies_count
docs: Total number of policies ever created for this user/mint combination
This field only increases and is used to prevent policy ID reuse

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: Account that paid rent for this account (receives rent on close)

fields.name: padding
docs: Reserved space for future extensions

types.name: UserPaymentCreated
docs: An event that is thrown when a user payment account is created

types.name: UserPaymentDeleted
docs: An event that is thrown when a user payment account is deleted

types.name: ValidationConfig
docs: Per-policy validation routing.
The pinned-account arity (`num_pinned_accounts`) and the pinned pubkeys
themselves live on the `ValidationPda` account, not here — they are
owner-declared at creation and replay-validated at execute (ADR-0016,
closes validation-gaming vector d). This struct only records which
validation program (Lighthouse) the policy is bound to; `Pubkey::default()`
is the "validation disabled" sentinel.
